findings.claim: The four historic-environment lessons each carried a 16-mark judgement question that this section never sets.
findings.truth: Two ways to fix it: (a) reframe each as a thematic 16-marker that spans periods and still uses the London material - what I have done - or (b) delete them and set a fourth 'Describe two features' instead. I recommend (a): it keeps a 16-mark essay in the bank for these lessons and teaches the link the specification builds between the historic environment and the thematic study.

summary: Every lesson carried exam-form errors: the thematic lessons (1-10) set 'Describe two features', 'Explain the importance' and 8-mark 'Explain why' questions that this paper never sets, and the historic-environment lessons (11-14) set a single invented source instead of a genuine pair plus a 16-mark essay this section does not have. All 60 practice questions were converted to the real forms with rebuilt mark schemes, and composed sources are now labelled as composed. On content, the worst errors were Russian breech-loading rifled artillery at Balaclava in 1854, 115 Cabinet meetings attributed to the Blitz alone, an invented '1990 Combined Cadet Force exclusion', the 'Hermann' bomb weight, Baedeker raids on London and a V2 on Deptford three days after the first strike.
